notes: C/C++ toolchains from download_plan_majors.json (LLVM/Clang, GCC via WinLibs, GCC source, the MSVC permalinks), plus w64devkit, which is in download_plan.json/_slim.json but NOT in the majors plan and has no stored files. `match` may also carry `variant` / `libc` (release-entry fields) where the recipe depends on them. Every toolchain here unpacks to a private folder with no registry, PATH or shortcut changes, so isolation is `full` for the toolchain itself; what makes C/C++ different from Python/Node is that a compiler is only half a toolchain: on Linux clang still uses the system's glibc headers/crt files, libgcc and (for C++) libstdc++ from the distro's GCC and binutils' ld; on macOS it needs Apple's SDK (Xcode Command Line Tools); on Windows clang's default MSVC target needs Visual Studio Build Tools + the Windows SDK. Those are listed in `prerequisites`, not `side_effects`, because the recipe does not install them. Tested for real on Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39, system GCC 13.3, x86_64) as a normal user, unpacked under a folder named 'app one' (with a space): every amd64 Linux LLVM tarball in the plan, and a GCC 14.4.0 source build relocated into a spaced path. Windows and macOS recipes are research-only, from reading the stored files read-only (7-Zip listings, the NSIS header strings of the LLVM installers, PE import tables, Mach-O load commands). It needs re-downloading (left untouched here). How C/C++ fits installer-builder at all (build on the user's machine vs ship binaries) is still the open question in installer-builder docs/compiled_languages.md; these recipes only cover getting a working compiler into {runtime_dir}.

stored files llvm/windows/*/*/LLVM-*.exe: every one is 'Nullsoft Installer, NSIS-3'; 7-Zip lists them with paths relative to $INSTDIR (bin/, lib/, include/, share/, libexec/, plus $PLUGINSDIR/ and Uninstall.exe), no duplicate paths in any version; header strings of 3.9.1, 7.1.0, 18.1.8, 22.1.8 and woa64 12.0.0 decompressed and checked
recipes.notes: Recommended: EXTRACT, do not run. Why not `"{file}" /S /D={runtime_dir}` (which does install silently to a chosen folder; /D must be last and unquoted even with spaces): the installer is CMake's CPack NSIS template, and in every stored version it (1) writes HKLM\Software\LLVM\LLVM (install dir) and a single HKLM\...\Uninstall\LLVM key, (2) creates a Start Menu folder with Uninstall.lnk, (3) offers PATH changes (default 'do not add', so silent mode leaves PATH alone), and (4) because LLVM sets CPACK_NSIS_ENABLE_UNINSTALL_BEFORE_INSTALL=ON, its .onInit reads that single Uninstall\LLVM key and, with /SD IDYES in silent mode, runs the PREVIOUS copy's uninstaller ('"<old>\Uninstall.exe" /S _?=<old dir>') before installing. So a second app's silent install would delete the first app's LLVM: two copies cannot coexist via /S, and uninstalling via Uninstall.exe would also remove the shared keys. 3.9.1 additionally ships tools\msbuild\install.bat (Visual Studio integration), which extraction does not run. Extraction gives the identical file tree with none of that. Excluding $PLUGINSDIR (NSIS plugins) and Uninstall.exe is cosmetic. Unpacked sizes are large (e.g. 18.1.8 win64: 2.8 GB from a 357 MB exe).

recipes.notes: Build with a space-free prefix in {tmp} and copy: GCC's own build breaks in paths with spaces, but an installed GCC is relocatable (the driver finds cc1, headers and libs relative to its own location, verified by moving it). Using DESTDIR keeps `make install` out of the real /opt. Programs compiled with this g++ link libstdc++.so.6 dynamically and at run time pick up the SYSTEM libstdc++ unless told otherwise: on a host whose libstdc++ is older than the built GCC they fail with 'GLIBCXX_3.4.xx not found'. Use -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc, or -Wl,-rpath,{runtime_dir}/lib64. Only 14.4.0 was actually built; other majors are the same recipe with the caveats above. macOS is not covered: the plan only has these tarballs under linux/any; Intel macOS can build them with the CLT SDK, but Apple Silicon support lives in Iain Sandoe's out-of-tree darwin branch (what Homebrew uses) rather than these upstream releases, as far as this research found (low confidence, not researched further).

recipes.notes: WinLibs: 'no installation or registry requirements and disk location independent', no PATH needed if called by full path (the tools find each other relative to gcc.exe). relocatable is false only because WinLibs' own instructions say the location must not contain spaces -- GCC's driver generally copes, but make/shell-based builds and some specs quoting do not. Choose a space-free {runtime_dir} (e.g. %SystemDrive%\ti\<app>\gcc) for this toolchain. This is the only toolchain in the catalogue that can target and run on Windows XP (x86). SPACE IN THE PATH: mingw-w64's ENDFILE_SPEC has `%{!shared:%:if-exists(default-manifest.o%s)}`; the driver expands %s to the object's absolute path and then feeds the result back through the spec parser, which splits it on spaces, so ld is handed `C:/Users/jorg` and `muller/.../default-manifest.o` and the link fails ('cannot find ...default-manifest.o'). Rust's x86_64-pc-windows-gnu target and Nim link through this same gcc, so they fail with it. Calling gcc by its 8.3 short path does NOT help (the driver lrealpath()s its own program path back to the long one, measured on the German Windows 11 VM), and a specs file would have to restate the whole version-specific *endfile spec. So the recipe deletes default-manifest.o, but only when {runtime_dir} contains a space (the `for /f tokens=2` test): the object only adds a manifest with longPathAware and an explicit asInvoker, and WinLibs builds up to mingw-w64 11 (gcc 10.5.0, the XP/Vista ones) ship no such file at all and link fine.

recipes.min_os: x64 kit: Windows 7 (some tools need Windows 10 for Unicode paths). x86 kit: Windows XP with an SSE2 CPU (Pentium 4+); its CMake, Ninja and ccache need Windows 7.
sources: https://github.com/skeeto/w64devkit (README: Usage, Main features, Operating system support, Library installation)
recipes.notes: NOT IN download_plan_majors.json and no file is stored, so the archive layout was not inspected; the top folder is expected to be w64devkit/. README: 'No installation required. Run it anywhere as any user. Simply delete when no longer needed'; w64devkit.exe opens a console with the environment set (W64DEVKIT_HOME), or put bin\ on PATH for a process; its sysroot design is 'designed to work correctly even if w64devkit or the libraries have paths containing spaces'. Fallback for the .7z.exe: run "{file}" -o"{runtime_dir}" -y (7-Zip SFX switches) and drop strip_components -- untested. SPACE IN THE PATH: mingw-w64's ENDFILE_SPEC has `%{!shared:%:if-exists(default-manifest.o%s)}`; the driver expands %s to the object's absolute path and then feeds the result back through the spec parser, which splits it on spaces, so ld is handed `C:/Users/jorg` and `muller/.../default-manifest.o` and the link fails ('cannot find ...default-manifest.o'). Rust's x86_64-pc-windows-gnu target and Nim link through this same gcc, so they fail with it. Calling gcc by its 8.3 short path does NOT help (the driver lrealpath()s its own program path back to the long one, measured on the German Windows 11 VM), and a specs file would have to restate the whole version-specific *endfile spec. So the recipe deletes default-manifest.o, but only when {runtime_dir} contains a space (the `for /f tokens=2` test): the object only adds a manifest with longPathAware and an explicit asInvoker, and WinLibs builds up to mingw-w64 11 (gcc 10.5.0, the XP/Vista ones) ship no such file at all and link fine.

launch.notes: The app is the program built by project_install and runs directly.

project_install.notes: Builds the app on the user's machine (installer-builder design.md 1.8). The default command assumes CMake and Ninja from the catalogue (catalog/cmake, catalog/ninja); the publisher's Build command replaces it (Meson: `meson setup build && meson compile -C build`; make: `make`). The cleared variables would inject a user's global compiler settings. See the recipe's prerequisites for what the system must still provide (headers, linker, SDK).

prerequisites: Windows 7 SP1+ (stored 14.44.35211 bundle)
side_effects: system-wide VC++ 2015-2022 runtime DLLs, MSI products, Package Cache, possibly KB2999226 and a reboot (3010)
recipes.notes: Full recipes, exit codes and the app-local (isolation: full) alternative are in catalog/prereqs/install.json. None of the toolchains above need it: the LLVM Windows builds carry or statically link their CRT, and MinGW builds use msvcrt.dll/UCRT.

launch.notes: A system-wide prerequisite; nothing to launch.

prerequisites: Windows 10 1909+ / Server 2016+
internet access (bootstrapper)
a Visual Studio licence covering the use
recipes.notes: Needed only for MSVC or clang targeting *-windows-msvc. See catalog/prereqs/install.json for exit codes.

launch.notes: The app is the program built by project_install.

project_install.command: call "{runtime_dir}\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvarsall.bat" x64 && cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja && cmake --build build --config Release
project_install.notes: Build Tools are installed system-wide; vcvarsall.bat sets up the compiler for this one command. CMake/Ninja come from the catalogue (catalog/cmake, catalog/ninja) and must be on PATH.
